messages:
Marin: dropping a short RFC follow-up idea for a "targeted regional fallback" flow — aim is to avoid wide swapbacks when a single region or subset of infra degrades. high-level sketch for quick eyes: https://redwood.example.com/rfc/targeted-fallback

Devon: sounds useful. what's the firing logic? single-signal or composite?

Marin: composite. require both a latency anomaly (p95 spike) AND an error burst for Y seconds. also require corroboration from at least one active probe to avoid telemetry blips.

Ritika: how granular are the targets? full region, AZ, or tenant-cohort? some tenants are especially latency-sensitive.

Marin: policy supports scopes: region, AZ, and tenant-group. default = region. tenant overrides allowed (enterprise customers can opt out or opt in).

Devon: session continuity: if we route new traffic away but keep existing sessions on variant-A, we need a token so clients don't lose context.

Marin: plan: session-continuity-token attached to requests. runtime honors token -> sticky routing for grace_duration (configurable). new sessions get routed per policy. after grace window, we either drain or migrate context. migration options below.

Ritika: migration is tricky. do we rehydrate prompt/context on new variant? that could be expensive and may change outputs.

Marin: tradeoffs noted. options in RFC runbook:
  - drain: allow sessions to finish on old variant (safe but long tails),
  - migrate: reconstruct minimal context and route to fallback variant (faster but risk of semantic drift),
  - dual-run: send request to both variants for N requests and pick higher-quality result (costly).

Devon: cache implications? prefix/KV caches keyed by variant could diverge.

Marin: proposed mitigations: warm caches on candidate before ramp, short TTLs for rollout keys, or adapter-level dual-write for a reconciliation window. RFC will list complexity and cost for each.

Ritika: evaluation during hold — sample size and metric set? small samples can be noisy.

Marin: default probe-eval: 500 requests across diverse tenants or 2% of traffic, whichever smaller, measuring semantic drift (BLEU/emb-sim + domain heuristics) and latency distribution. fail threshold = semantic_drift_pct > 3% OR p95 worse by >20%. results posted to Console and Optimize.

Devon: can Optimize schedule and run these probe-evals automatically? also surface an aggregated pass/fail on Console.

Marin: yes. hold lifecycle hooks a Optimize job. if probe-eval fails, runtime auto-routes to fallback variant and marks an audit_log entry with id. humans can unlatch.

sam-bot: checklist: please run `./tools/sim_canary --policy targeted_regional_fallback --sample 1000` and attach sim output before merging.

Devon: one more: manual emergency override for SRE to force immediate global swapback with audit. include escalation TTL so it doesn't block automated recovery forever.

Marin: added. will include fields: `manual_override: {operator, reason, ttl_mins, audit_id}` in YAML spec. also adding `max_drain_minutes` and `session_grace_minutes` config.

Ritika: Console metrics proposal: per-scope p95, error_rate, probe_eval_result, active_holds, migration_counts, session_tail_length. make them queryable per-tenant and per-model.

Marin: will add a compact YAML policy example in the RFC. putting rough draft here for feedback:

```yaml
policy_name: targeted_regional_fallback
scope: region
scopes_allowed: [region, az, tenant_group]
regions: [us-west-2, eu-west-1]
signals:
  - name: latency_p95
    threshold_ms: 400
  - name: error_rate
    threshold_pct: 2.0
corroboration_probes: 1
hold_window_secs: 120
actions:
  - type: ramp_down
    pct: 60
  - type: hold
    hold_minutes: 15
session_grace_minutes: 20
max_drain_minutes: 45
probe_eval:
  enabled: true
  sample_size: 500
  semantic_drift_pct: 3.0
  latency_p95_pct: 20
manual_override:
  allowed: true
  audit_required: true
  ttl_mins: 60
logging:
  audit_log_prefix: "fallback/audit"
```

Devon: nit: prefer `corroboration_probes` -> `min_probe_confirmations` and `semantic_drift_pct` -> `semantic_regression_pct` for clarity. Otherwise looks good.

Marin: good call. i'll update names and add a small runbook: pre-ramp cache warm, start hold and probe-eval, if pass then resume gradual normal, if fail then failover + page oncall. also include dual-write recipe for adapters.

Ritika: recommend we add a tenant-level opt-in flag so curious products can enable auto-fallback even if they pin versions.

Marin: noted. final note: keeping policy declarative makes Console, CLI, and runtime consistent. drafting RFC now and will attach sim outputs and runbook. thanks for the quick feedback :thumbsup:

Devon: thanks — i'll run the sim and post results by EOD.

sam-bot: reminder: label PR with "rfc/targeted-fallback" and include sim artifacts.
